skill.name: api-fuzzing-bug-bounty
skill.description: Guide authorized API security testing for REST, SOAP, and GraphQL services. It covers reconnaissance, fuzzing, IDOR, injection, authentication, and GraphQL abuse cases.
skill.summary: Structured API fuzzing guidance for authorized bug bounty and penetration testing work.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby shell findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline examples, not executable backtick calls. The skill still contains confirmed high-risk dual-use guidance for sensitive file disclosure, SSRF, IDOR, authentication abuse, injection, and DoS testing. I found no prompt injection attempt.

remediation.suggestion: Remove direct /etc/passwd and web.config examples or replace them with harmless lab-only placeholders and explicit authorization warnings.

remediation.issue: SSRF, port scanning, and tracking examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace loopback port probes and IP logger references with non-routable lab examples, and require scope confirmation before any network test.
Reframe IDOR examples around owned test accounts and synthetic data, and remove references to other users' sensitive data.

remediation.issue: Rate limit bypass and DoS guidance
remediation.suggestion: Add safe request limits, stop conditions, and lab-only constraints for batching and nested query tests.
Replace target.com and attacker.com style examples with reserved documentation domains or named placeholders.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthorized Data Access Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill explains IDOR testing, GraphQL access to other user data, and modified invoice requests that reveal another user's records. This can support business-logic abuse outside an authorized scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple sections explicitly describe accessing other users, sensitive fields, and invoice data by changing identifiers. The authorized-use note lowers misuse certainty, but the exploit intent is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Authentication and Rate Limit Abuse Guidance

content.user_title: Test API Security With Guided Fuzzing
content.value_statement: API testing can miss auth, IDOR, and parser weaknesses across REST, SOAP, and GraphQL surfaces. This skill gives structured checklists and payload ideas for authorized API security assessments.
actual_capabilities: Maps REST, SOAP, and GraphQL testing workflows from recon to reporting.
Provides checks for authentication, IDOR, SQL injection, command injection, XXE, SSRF, and method tampering.
Includes GraphQL introspection, batching, nested query, and XSS testing guidance.
Summarizes API security tools, wordlists, and Burp extensions for manual testing.
Lists constraints for testing mobile, web, developer, and versioned APIs separately.
Gives troubleshooting tips for empty responses, disabled introspection, and endpoint discovery.
limitations: It does not confirm that a target is in scope or legally authorized.
It does not automate scanning, exploit execution, or report generation.
It includes offensive payload examples that require expert judgment.
It cannot validate findings without live target evidence and permission.

use_cases.title: Scope an API assessment
use_cases.description: Build a structured test plan for a scoped REST, SOAP, or GraphQL target before manual testing begins.

use_cases.title: Validate API defenses
use_cases.description: Check authentication, authorization, parser, and rate-limit controls during an internal security review.

use_cases.title: Train controlled labs
use_cases.description: Teach common API vulnerability classes with clear workflows, expected evidence, and safe testing boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Recon Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a scoped API review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized API reconnaissance checklist for a scoped REST service. Include documentation sources, version checks, and safe endpoint enumeration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan IDOR Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate authorization testing with test accounts
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan IDOR tests for a scoped API using two test accounts. Include expected evidence and reporting notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review GraphQL Exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess a scoped GraphQL endpoint for introspection, batching, authorization gaps, and query depth risks. Keep recommendations defensive and bounded.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full API Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete authorized API security test plan for REST and GraphQL services. Cover auth, IDOR, injection, SSRF, rate limits, DoS safeguards, and evidence handling.

output_examples.input: Request: create a safe API recon plan for a staging service.
output_examples.output: A phased checklist covering documentation review, version discovery, endpoint enumeration, authentication mapping, and stopping conditions.

output_examples.input: Request: summarize IDOR testing for two authorized accounts.
Request: review GraphQL risk areas before testing.
output_examples.output: A concise review of introspection, field authorization, batching, depth controls, and safe test limits.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, rate limits, and data handling rules before testing.
Use owned test accounts and lab data when probing authorization boundaries.
Document exact requests, responses, impact, and remediation guidance for each finding.
anti_patterns: Testing real users, production data, or third-party services without explicit approval.
Running high-volume fuzzing or nested queries without rate and impact limits.
Copying payloads against public placeholder domains instead of scoped targets.

faq.question: Is this skill only for bug bounty work?
faq.answer: No. It also supports authorized penetration tests, internal assessments, and controlled training labs.

faq.question: Does it run scanning tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides manual workflows and examples. The user must run approved tools in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it test GraphQL APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers introspection, batching, IDOR, injection, XSS, and query depth risks.

faq.question: Does it replace a formal API security methodology?
faq.answer: No. It is a practical checklist that should align with scope, rules of engagement, and internal standards.

faq.question: What permissions are required before use?
faq.answer: Written authorization, target scope, test accounts, rate limits, and data handling rules should be confirmed first.

faq.question: Why is the audit risk elevated?
faq.answer: The skill includes offensive examples for file disclosure, SSRF, IDOR, injection, rate-limit abuse, and DoS testing.
